title: Interactive 3D Periodic Table with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that displays an interactive 3D periodic table with atomic particle visualizations.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 30) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights from (10,10,10) and (-10,5,-10).
- Dark background color (#0a0a1a).
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation/zoom.

## Periodic Table Layout
- Create the first 36 elements (H through Kr) as 3D boxes (BoxGeometry 0.8x0.8x0.2) arranged in the standard periodic table grid layout.
- Each element box should be colored by its category: alkali metals (#ff6b6b), alkaline earth (#ffa94d), transition metals (#74c0fc), metalloids (#a9e34b), nonmetals (#69db7c), noble gases (#da77f2), halogens (#ffd43b), other metals (#4dabf7).
- Each box face should display the element symbol as a text sprite or canvas texture.
- Position the table centered at origin, with each cell spaced 1.1 units apart in X and 1.1 units apart in Y.

## Element Data
- Store element data: symbol, name, atomicNumber, atomicMass, category, electronConfig (number of electrons per shell as array), protons, neutrons for at least the first 36 elements.

## Selection & Info Panel
- Clicking on an element box selects it (highlight with emissive glow or outline).
- Show a DOM info panel (top-right, 280px wide) displaying: symbol, name, atomic number, atomic mass, category, and electron configuration.
- Add a 'Show Atom' button in the info panel.

## 3D Atom Visualization (Particle Mode)
- When 'Show Atom' is clicked, transition to atom view:
  - Hide the periodic table (set visible=false).
  - Show a 3D atom model at origin:
    - Nucleus: cluster of small red spheres (protons) and blue spheres (neutrons), slightly randomized positions within radius 0.5.
    - Electrons: green small spheres orbiting in shells. Shell radii: shell1=2, shell2=3.5, shell3=5, shell4=6.5. Each electron orbits at a unique angle offset, rotating around the nucleus.
    - Add particle trail effect: each electron leaves a fading trail (use a Points system or line with decreasing opacity) showing its orbital path as a glowing ring.
  - Electrons should animate continuously, orbiting at speed proportional to 1/shellRadius.
- Add a 'Back to Table' button to return to the periodic table view.

## Category Filter
- Add a DOM dropdown (id='categoryFilter') with options: 'All', 'Alkali Metals', 'Alkaline Earth', 'Transition Metals', 'Metalloids', 'Nonmetals', 'Noble Gases', 'Halogens', 'Other Metals'.
- Filtering hides non-matching elements (visible=false) and shows matching ones.

## Keyboard Interactions
- Press 'R' to reset camera to initial position (0,5,30).
- Press 'T' to toggle rotation animation of the entire periodic table (slow Y-axis rotation at 0.005 rad/frame).
- Press 'P' to toggle particle trail visibility on/off when in atom view.
- Press '1','2','3','4' to highlight only electrons in that shell number (others dim to 0.2 opacity).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- selectedElement: null or {symbol, atomicNumber, name, category} of currently selected element
- viewMode: 'table' | 'atom'
- tableRotating: boolean (default false)
- categoryFilter: string (current filter, default 'All')
- visibleElementCount: number of currently visible element boxes
- atomData: null or {protons, neutrons, electrons, shells} when in atom view (shells = number of occupied shells)
- electronAnimating: boolean (true when atom view is active and electrons orbit)
- particleTrailsVisible: boolean (default true)
- highlightedShell: 0 (0 means all shells shown, 1-4 for specific shell)
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z} updated each frame
- totalElements: 36
- frameCount: number incremented each animation frame

## Animation
- Use requestAnimationFrame loop. Increment frameCount each frame.
- In atom view, rotate electrons around Y axis at their respective speeds.
- Update cameraPosition each frame from camera.position.
physics_constraints: Electrons must orbit at speeds inversely proportional to shell radius. Nucleus particles must stay within radius 0.5 of center. Electron shell radii must be 2, 3.5, 5, 6.5 for shells 1-4. All positions must be NaN-free.
